listing.name: Mage Bros. / Mage Bros. Native
listing.summary: Play the original Mage Bros. levels with widescreen, modern controls and local co-op.

steps.title: Keep the original Mage Bros. files together
steps.instruction: Get the freeware 2.0 release from Saito Games, using the publisher link in the setup guide. Keep MageBros.exe and Music01.mid through Music06.mid together. The native engine checks the original executable before reading its game data.

steps.title: Start the native Windows engine
steps.instruction: Extract the Windows x64 package into a writable folder. Run MageBrosNative.exe with --game followed by the quoted path to the original MageBros.exe. Use Windows 10 or 11 with OpenGL 3.3. If Windows reports missing MSVCP140.dll or VCRUNTIME140.dll, install Microsoft’s Visual C++ v14 x64 Redistributable.

warnings: The upstream package includes reconstructed Mage Bros. and DirectX framework code. The MIT grant covers the port’s own code. Rights to the reconstructed code remain with their original owners.
Mage Bros. Native keeps its own progress. Start a new native save if you previously played the original game.

references.title: Keep settings and progress before replacing the engine
references.instruction: Close the game and copy magebros_native.ini and your screenshots from the engine directory. Back up %APPDATA%/MageBrosNative/saves/original or the folder you chose in save_path. Keep the original executable and music in their own folder.

references.title: Build for Apple Silicon or a Linux handheld
references.instruction: The publisher’s build guide covers Apple Silicon on macOS 12 or later and the R36S Linux handheld. The Apple Silicon build stores settings and saves under ~/Library/Application Support/MageBrosNative. The R36S needs the original files and a General MIDI SoundFont for music. The tagged release provides a ready-made package for Windows.
